title: Sum of Sortable Integers
summary: Given an integer array nums of length n, determine all integers k that divide n and enable nums to be sorted in non-decreasing order by partitioning nums into consecutive subarrays of length k and independently rotating each subarray.
statement: Given an integer array nums of length n, determine all integers k that divide n and enable nums to be sorted in non-decreasing order by partitioning nums into consecutive subarrays of length k and independently rotating each subarray. Return the sum of all such integers k.
constraints: For a divisor k of n, split nums into blocks of length k and rotate each block independently.
Sum every k for which these rotations can make the whole array nondecreasing.
reference_solution:
def sum_sortable_block_sizes(nums):
    target=sorted(nums)
    def rotation_equal(source,wanted):
        if not source:return True
        pattern=wanted;prefix=[0]*len(pattern)
        for i in range(1,len(pattern)):
            j=prefix[i-1]
            while j and pattern[i]!=pattern[j]:j=prefix[j-1]
            if pattern[i]==pattern[j]:j+=1
            prefix[i]=j
        matched=0
        for value in (source+source)[:-1]:
            while matched and value!=pattern[matched]:matched=prefix[matched-1]
            if value==pattern[matched]:matched+=1
            if matched==len(pattern):return True
        return False
    answer=0
    for size in range(1,len(nums)+1):
        if len(nums)%size==0 and all(rotation_equal(nums[i:i+size],target[i:i+size]) for i in range(0,len(nums),size)):answer+=size
    return answer

hints: The final nondecreasing array is uniquely sorted(nums).
For each divisor k, every source block must independently be a cyclic rotation of the corresponding target block.
Test rotation equality by searching the target block in source+source with a prefix-function matcher.
Blocks cannot exchange elements, so the per-block rotation condition is both necessary and sufficient; summing passing divisors gives the answer.
